description: root@vm
title: root@vm

description:
`scripts/check-wasm.sh` cannot detect unresolved external symbols, because it checks rather than builds. Found 2026-09-14.

## The defect

Line 119:

    err=$(cargo check -q -p "$c" --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown 2>&1)

`cargo check` runs rustc with `--emit=metadata`. **It does not invoke the
linker.** Any `extern "C"` declaration therefore type-checks fine and the gate
passes, whether or not the symbol exists on the target.

Concretely: the workspace has six `extern "C"` blocks calling erf / erfc /
tgamma / lgamma (op-chyp.6), in outram-foam-basic-lib, tampines-steam-tables
and outram-park-fork-coolprop — all three of which the gate reports as passing
for wasm32-unknown-unknown. wasm32-unknown-unknown has no system libc.

## Why this is worth recording rather than just fixing

CLAUDE.md's wasm section is unusually honest already — it states "COMPILING IS
NOT RUNNING", explains that thread::spawn / Instant / fs all compile and fail
at runtime, and names chem-eng as the standing proof. It also documents the
`--lib`-only limitation and why `--all-targets` is not usable.

It does NOT document this one, which sits a layer below: **checking is not even
linking**. A reader of that section would reasonably believe the gate at least
proves the symbols resolve. It does not.

## Options, not yet decided

1. Switch the gate to `cargo build --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
   Catches link errors; costs real compile time on every run.
2. Keep `cargo check` for speed and add a separate, less frequent link check.
3. Keep as-is and document the limitation in CLAUDE.md's wasm section
   alongside the existing caveats.

At minimum do (3) — the section's value comes from being candid about what the
gate does and does not prove, and this is a gap in that candour.

## NOT verified

Whether a real wasm build actually fails on those six blocks. wasm32 is not an
installed target on this host. Rust's wasm std may or may not export those C
symbols. Verify before asserting either way — install the target and run
`cargo build --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p outram-foam-basic-lib`.
title: check-wasm.sh cannot catch unresolved extern symbols — it checks, never links

description: Observed 2026-09-17. A bad upstream transient (core over-cooling) drove the steam-generator tube side to 273.143 K at 4 MPa and the IF97 (p,T) flash panicked with 'out of bounds'. That is not a physical state: the condenser is at 7 kPa (T_sat ~39 degC) and feedwater enters at 104 degC, so nothing in the cycle is colder than ~39 degC and the water has nowhere colder to go. The energy balance has no floor at its own cold boundary, so it integrates past it and only stops when the steam tables refuse. Needs an explicit asserted invariant in the same spirit as the_helium_never_leaves_the_core_hotter_than_the_bed: the tube side cannot fall below the colder of the feedwater inlet and the condenser saturation temperature. Independent of the decay-heat-path sizing bug that triggered it.
title: htgr_sim_v1 secondary has no cold-boundary floor: tube side can walk to the IF97 triple point

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
NOT APPLICABLE TO H-in-H2O -- settled from NJOY2016's source, 2026-09-13.

This bead is the missing secondary-scatterer SCT term for B(7)=0 evaluations. I went
looking for it as an explanation for gh:#188's water deficit being twice graphite's
(water has a secondary scatterer, graphite has none). It is not that.

From njoy/NJOY2016 src/thermr.f90, calcem:
  sb2=0 ; az2=0
  if (ni.gt.6) then
     if (scr(13).eq.zero) az2=scr(15)          ! scr(13) is B(7)
     if (az2.ne.zero) sb2=scr(14)*((az2+1)/az2)**2
     sb2=sb2/scr(18)/natom
  endif
and from the tape, tsl-HinH2O MF=7/MT=4 has NI=12, NS=1 and
  B(7) = 1, B(8) = 3.7939, B(9) = 15.8575, B(12) = 1.
B(7) = 1 is non-zero, so az2 stays zero and sb2 = 0. NJOY does NOT fold the free-gas
oxygen into MT=222 for water; it is handled outside THERMR, exactly as
sct_double_differential's doc comment already claimed. The committed NJOY goldens are
therefore like-for-like with this port's MT=222.

The bead stays open on its own terms -- some polyethylene evaluations do set B(7)=0 --
but it is not a candidate for gh:#188 and should not be picked up in that hope.

title: THERMR: secondary-scatterer SCT term for B(7)=0 evaluations (teff2)

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-10 (session_01AhE6XBx3nRd81aHLQrciQe): FIRST GOLDEN-FILE VALIDATION of the ported GROUPR engine against a real NJOY2016 GENDF tape - the "top V&V ask" of op-3ut/op-cpz/op-ini is now measured, for the vector (mfd=3) path with the Bondarenko self-shielded flux (nsigz>1).

Oracle: NJOY2016 ac5adf5 (2016.79) built in-session; RECONR(0.001)/BROADR(293.6 K)/GROUPR on ENDF/B-VIII.0 U-238 (MAT 9237), ign=1 (29 user groups 1e-5..2e7 eV), iwt=3 (1/E), lord=0, sigz = 1e10 1e4 1e3 1e2 10 1, MT 1/2/18/102. Golden GENDF (35 KB) + the exact deck committed at reference-data/gendf/ (README with provenance); new accessor reference_data::reference_file("gendf", ..) (+ OUTRAM_PARK_REFERENCE_DATA_DIR override). Test: crates/njoy-outram-park-fork/tests/groupr_u238_gendf_golden.rs (methodology + results in its doc comment).

Upstream read before measuring: getwtf iwt=3 -> wtf=1/e, enext=1.01*e (groupr.f90:5203); genflx nsigz>1 tabulates wtf*(sigpot+sigz)/(sigt+sigz) on the greedy union of 1% steps and the MT=1 grid (:5623-5665), getflx interpolates it lin-lin (:6478-6490); sigpot=0 unless iwt<0 (:4978); lord=0 with nsigz>1 promotes MT=1 to NL=2 (P0+P1, :6498-6499), other MTs stay NL=1; panel = trapezoid flux + rate-linear-across-panel (:5858-6091) == our group_integral. Prediction stated before measuring: <1e-5 with NJOY's own PENDF, O(1e-3) with the crate's RECONR/BROADR.

MEASURED (all 29 groups x 6 sigma0):
 Tier 1, engine isolated on NJOY's own PENDF (env OUTRAM_PARK_NJOY_U238_PENDF; 155,207 sigt points -> 156,864 flux points, NJOY listing: 156,854): max |dsigma_g/sigma_g| = 6.85e-7 (MT=1), 4.55e-7 (MT=2), 2.07e-6 (MT=18), 2.65e-6 (MT=102, group 9, sigma0=inf); max group-flux dev 4.93e-7 (= the 7-significant-figure storage floor). PASS at 1e-5. The group-averaging engine (genflx_bondarenko + panel/group_integral + self_shielded_group_xs) reproduces NJOY.
 Tier 2, crate RECONR(0.001)+BROADR(293.6 K) from the committed ENDF tape (961,139 sigt points; 156 s): max dev 1.98e-4 (MT=1), 1.98e-4 (MT=2), 9.24e-4 (MT=102), flux 6.06e-5 -> PASS at 3e-3. MT=18 1.14e-2 (group 13, 40-50 eV, sigma_f ~2.5e-7 b). Read upstream: reconr.f90:109-117, 428-430 - where a point's resonance-integral contribution is below errint = err/20000 = 5e-8 b, NJOY converges it only to errmax = 10*err = 1 % (NJOY listing: 363,092 points "affected by resonance integral check"). Sub-threshold U-238 fission sits entirely under that floor, so the 1.1 % is NJOY's own linearization slack, not an engine defect (tier 1 shows 2e-6 on MT=18 with NJOY's grid). Asserted at 3e-2 for MT=18, 3e-3 otherwise.

NOT covered (still open): the matrix path (mfd=6 scatter matrices, File-6 feeds, op-ini's port half), URR self-shielding via MT=152 (no UNRESR step in this deck - op-cpz's read_urr_table half), GAMINR, lord>0.

Side findings (filed separately): crate RECONR lacks the errint/errmax resonance-integral relaxation (961k vs NJOY 448k points at the same err); crate BROADR does no thinning (NJOY 448,168 -> 155,207 at errthn=0.001).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-10, later the same session (session_01AhE6XBx3nRd81aHLQrciQe): the MT=152 half is now measured too, and it found a port defect.

Second oracle run: same U-238 deck with `unresr 20 22 24 / 9237 1 6 1 / 293.6 / 1e10 1e4 1e3 1e2 10 1 / 0 /` between BROADR and GROUPR (golden reference-data/gendf/u238-ENDF8.0-293.6K-29g-iwt3-6sigz-unresr.gendf + deck). GROUPR's stounr found MF=2/MT=152 (no "no unresolved sigma zero data" message this time). Rust side: read_urr_from_tape(Some(&pendf), 9237, 1, 293.6) -> UnresolvedTable, fed to self_shielded_group_xs (tier 3 of tests/groupr_u238_gendf_golden.rs, env OUTRAM_PARK_NJOY_U238_UNRESR_PENDF).

Read upstream first: genflx (groupr.f90:5636-5650) sets tot(iz)=sigt(e) for every iz, calls getunr(1,e,en,tot) so that INSIDE the URR tot(iz) becomes the MT=152 self-shielded total for sigz(iz), and only then forms fac=(sigpot+sigz)/(tot(iz)+sigz). Our genflx_bondarenko used the smooth sigma_t.value(e). Predicted before measuring: URR-group flux low by up to ~10 % at sigz=1 b, sigma_g nearly unchanged (second order).

Measured BEFORE the fix: group 22 (20-50 keV) flux at sigz=1 b 6.78 % LOW (ours 0.062356 vs NJOY 0.066892); sigma_g within 1.48e-3 (MT=102, group 22) / 3.43e-3 (MT=18). Sign and size as predicted.
Fix (commit cf9759f1): unresolved::genflx_bondarenko_urr(sigma_t, urr, weight, sigpot, dilutions, grid) shields the total through UnresolvedTable::shield(UrrReaction::Total, ..) per dilution before the Bondarenko factor; genflx_bondarenko is its urr=None wrapper (numerically unchanged, tier 1 re-run identical); self_shielded_group_xs now uses it.
Measured AFTER: sigma_g within 2.65e-6 (MT=102, group 9), 2.07e-6 (MT=18), group flux within 4.93e-7 - the maxima are back in resolved-range groups, i.e. the URR groups agree to NJOY's 7-figure storage floor. groupr:: lib tests 77/77 still pass.

What this validates: read_urr_from_tape (tape-locate + LIST decode), UnresolvedTable::shield (stounr/getunr incl. the LSSF=1 multiplicative combine), and the URR-shielded Bondarenko flux - for U-238 (LSSF=1) at one temperature, six sigz, lord=0. Not covered: LSSF=0 materials, multiple temperatures, lord>0, the flux-calculator (iwt<0) path, the matrix path.

description:
Small structural unblock with large leverage. The TUAS Material enum is solid-or-liquid only, so the entire TUAS prebuilt component library cannot currently be used for a helium loop — which is most of what an HTR-10 primary circuit is.

SCOPE: add a gas variant and wire it through the property dispatch so gas-phase components resolve density, viscosity, conductivity and heat capacity. Helium properties should route to crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop, which already carries a full Helmholtz EOS plus real NIST-lineage viscosity and conductivity correlations, tested against tabulated reference states.

Note the related defect: htgr_sim_v1 currently hardcodes a constant helium viscosity despite the real correlation existing one crate away. Fix that as part of this.

Adding an enum variant will produce compile errors at every match site — that is the design working as intended. Work through them.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
CORRECTED BY THE MAINTAINER 2026-08-11 — THIS BEAD AS WRITTEN IS WRONG. DO NOT IMPLEMENT IT.

Maintainer ruling: TUAS should NEVER have a gas arm. That was never its intent — tuas_boussinesq_solver is for SALT solvers only. Its Material enum being solid-or-liquid is a deliberate scope boundary, not an oversight, and adding a gas variant would widen a crate past its designed purpose.

GAS BELONGS IN tampines, which is the central thermal-hydraulic framework and already composes tuas, outram-park-fork-coolprop, tampines-steam-tables, outram-foam-basic-lib and chem-eng. Helium properties already exist in outram-park-fork-coolprop (full Helmholtz EOS plus real NIST-lineage viscosity and conductivity correlations, tested against tabulated reference states), so the work is exposing them through tampines rather than duplicating them.

The underlying NEED is still real — an HTR-10 primary circuit is a helium loop and nothing in the workspace can currently represent one with prebuilt components. But the fix is a tampines-side gas component layer, not a TUAS enum variant. See the replacement bead.

Note this also affects the framing of the earlier scoping document: docs/reactor-scoping/htr10.md lists 'Gas arm in the TUAS material enum' under MISSING with the note that the whole TUAS prebuilt component library cannot be used for a helium loop. That entry should be rewritten to point at tampines when someone next edits that file.

title: HTR-10: add a gas arm to the TUAS Material enum

description:
Candidate 1 of op-qho6. Build a DETERMINISTIC, independent reference for resonance absorption in a lump at realistic optical thickness (ring-RPT fuel annulus 1.4934-1.7531 cm, ~6.6 mfp at the 6.674 eV U-238 peak), where examples/lump_self_shielding_scan.rs currently has NO oracle beyond the transparent limit.

Method: first-flight collision probabilities for concentric spheres by exact impact-parameter track quadrature, white-boundary closure P_ij = P_ij0 + P_iS P_Sj/(1-P_SS), then a multi-region slowing-down solve on the same lethargy grid machinery as physics::slowing_down::solve_on_grid. Verified against the closed-form sphere escape probability P_esc(x) = 3/(4x)[1 - 1/(2x^2) + (1/x + 1/(2x^2))e^{-2x}], reciprocity 4 V_i Sigma_i P_iS = A P_Si, conservation, and the homogeneous limit. Flat flux per sub-region is the only approximation; convergence demonstrated by shell refinement.

Compared against LumpCellMc (the real CSG transport) on the same geometry.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-12 progress. Module physics::collision_probability built and verified against closed forms: bare-sphere escape probability 1.5e-13 (48 Gauss nodes, x=1e-3..1e2), surface reciprocity 4 V_i Sigma_i P_iS = A P_Si 3.7e-16, white-closure conservation 8.9e-16, sub-shell invariance 4.4e-16. Gauss-Legendre generator checked on even moments to 1.7e-14. tests/lump_collision_probability.rs, 4 gates, all pass.

physics::slowing_down::solve_deterministic_multiregion built on it. EXACT TEST: a shell cell filled with ONE material must return the infinite-medium answer identically. It does, to 1.1e-12 relative, at cell radii 0.01 / 1 / 100 cm and 3 / 9 / 24 shells, worst conservation defect 1.6e-14.

Flat-flux convergence measured, not assumed: fuel sub-shells 1->16, the lumping effect L converges geometrically; at 12 sub-shells the residual is <0.02% at 2.6 mfp and <0.15% at 25.7 mfp. Moderator subdivision worth <=0.026%; quadrature 16->32 nodes worth nothing.

FIRST MEASUREMENT (60k histories, seed 0xABCD_0003): MC vs the deterministic reference on the same cell -- 0.10 mfp -0.27%, 0.86 mfp -0.00%, 2.57 mfp -0.67%, 8.56 mfp -0.61%, 25.69 mfp +0.57%; worst 1.4 sigma. High-statistics run under way.

notes.content:
RESULT (2026-09-12, commit 89050556). The candidate is RULED OUT.

MEASUREMENT, MODE=thick HIST=50000 -> 200 000 histories/row, seed 0xABCD_0003,
exact homogeneous p_esc = 0.38763:

  R/mfp   MC p_esc   1 sigma    ORACLE   MC - ORACLE     z
   2.57    0.39811   0.00109   0.40013     -0.50 %    -1.84
   8.56    0.43320   0.00111   0.43180     +0.32 %    +1.26
  25.69    0.50082   0.00112   0.50059     +0.05 %    +0.20

Worst 1.8 sigma over a range where the lumping effect itself grows from +2.7 %
to +29.2 % of the homogeneous answer. No trend with optical thickness, no
consistent sign.

ON THE REAL RING-RPT ANNULUS (1.4934-1.7531 cm at its own radii, 6.65 mfp thick
at the 6.674 eV peak, a SHELL so the chord distribution is the pebble's own,
200 000 histories, seed 0xABCD_0004):

  volume-homogenised exact p_esc                0.673208
  MONTE CARLO    p_esc 0.797250 +/- 0.000899    fuel absorption 0.201380
  DETERMINISTIC  p_esc 0.798467                 fuel absorption 0.200160
  lumping effect L     MC 0.124042 vs 0.125259  -0.97 % +/- 0.72 %

-> -32 +/- 24 pcm of the pebble's +3327 pcm of lumping reactivity, against a
+4004 pcm residual. Reproducing the residual this way needs the lumping effect
to be wrong by MORE THAN 100 %.

THE SIGN IS ALSO WRONG. 'Under-absorbing in the resonance range' means too much
self-shielding: p_esc too HIGH, fuel absorption too LOW. Measured is the
opposite -- the MC absorbs 0.61 % MORE in the fuel annulus than the reference,
at 1.3 sigma.
